reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared features across instances with quantified feature attributions from XAI tools to validate and strengthen the hypothesis of spurious correlations. This ensures both pattern discovery and model-level evidence of high attribution despite semantic irrelevance.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify the exact column names that appear in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 35024) by cross-referencing their input feature sets.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared feature columns across all three instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether the shared features have semantic plausibility in relation to income prediction, considering factors like age, education, marital status, and workclass.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: An assessment of whether the shared features are semantically related to income class, indicating potential spuriousness

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides game-theoretic feature importance that reveals if a given feature drives predictions despite being semantically unrelated. LIME offers local interpretability, helping confirm spurious influence in individual instances. Integrated Gradients offer gradient-based attribution across instances for robustness. Sensitivity analysis quantifies impact by removing features, confirming their undue influence on misclassification. Together, they validate the spuriousness of shared features beyond just presence.
